# Orch v0.1.2

API keys have their own HTTP and WebSocket surface, and background activity uses
the current reader's access for both browser and key connections.

## Before deployment

- Browser sessions use `/api/v1`; keys use `/openapi/v1`, including
  `/openapi/v1/ws`. Update key clients to the key prefix. Review any retained
  `nginx.conf` and outer proxy against the shipped key-route blocks: the updater
  preserves existing configuration. Forward both prefixes unchanged and permit
  both WebSocket roots. Installer downloads remain at `/api/v1/downloads/`.
- This candidate contains the complete PostgreSQL 17 schema for a fresh
  installation. Its released SQL bytes are recorded in `migrations/RELEASED` in
  the source. A database made from an earlier development schema may have
  different migration checksums; there is no automatic rewrite of its migration
  history. Qualify a compatible upgrade or restore before using it with this
  release. See the [migration policy](../../migrations/README.md).
- Preserve the deployment's data, configuration and secrets. Use the verified
  payloads for the host architecture; [deployment and recovery](../../deploy/README.md)
  describes first start, update, backup and rollback.

## Release contents

The release carries both Linux server, CLI and node architectures, the shared
browser application, deployment scripts and operator documentation. Every server
contains the full schema, pinned model rates and downloads for all five connector
targets: Linux x86-64/ARM64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon and Windows x86-64. Windows
on ARM uses the x86-64 connector through emulation.

The pipeline verifies the exact source schema and deployment bundle, assembles
both server architectures, and publishes only after full CI is green for the
release tag and commit. Optional environment images require a separate approved
run. The [release guide](../../docs/operator/releases.md) describes the snapshot
rehearsal and the publication gates.
